paragraphs: R' Yehoshua ben Levi bar Shalom.
Hyman cites Vayikra Rabbah 15:16. He says that without doubt the text had read R. Y. HaLevi, whom he identifies as R’ Yehudah HaLevi bar Shalom, well known in aggadic literature.

notes.text: The source prints unexplained בל״ם and כטוב where the context suggests “written.” This remains a source question; “well known in aggadic literature” is an idiom, not a book title Shaarei Aggadah.

Supplied בל״ם remains unexplained and is not silently replaced by בל״ס or expanded as without doubt. כטוב is contextually read as written alongside the older OCR כתוב, without a new glyph inspection. The chapter15 and finite full-name nonmatch reports are inherited research, not new universal absence proof. Hyman owns the Yehudah HaLevi reconstruction, and well known in aggadic literature remains an idiom rather than an identified book. The supplied פט״ו-טז is conventionally15:16, not a proved modern occurrence; all three personal-title abbreviations remain R'.

Hyman’s print (vol. II, p. 646) reads ובל״ס היה כתוב, “and without doubt it had been written,” where the supplied transcription has ובל״ם היה כטוב. Bamidbar Rabbah 15:16 names Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi berabbi Shalom in its account of Ruth and Boaz. Buber’s Tanchuma, Shmini 7, names R’ Yehudah HaLevi bar Shalom in a separate homily about wine. The identification is Hyman’s.
